title: [finding] dashboard `renderFieldValue` reads any `format` containing Y/M/D/H/m/s as a date pattern — a text field hinted `format: 'email'` goes to `formatDate` and its value is hidden in the dashboard table and record drawer
body:
① — a user-visible value disappears.

Filed from `objectstack-ai/objectstack`'s `domain:spec` execution seat 1 (`session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`), because the fix lands here. ⛔ Unlabelled beyond `finding`, ⛔ ungraded, ⛔ unrouted — routing is this repo's triage. Surfaced by objectstack PR #19763's round-2 reader census for `FieldSchema.format`; the branch selection below re-read at source by the filing seat.

## At the pinned `.objectui-sha` `87af769e9a3ee28ace099fdd653d3ebd79fe82e2`

`packages/plugin-dashboard/src/recordFields.tsx` — the field meta carries the object field's own `format` (`format: overrides.format ?? meta?.format`, ~`:334`), and `renderFieldValue` then decides:

```ts
if (typeof fmt === 'string' && /[YMDHms]/.test(fmt)) {
  return formatDate(value, fmt);
}
const Renderer = getCellRenderer(resolveCellRendererType(fieldMeta as any));
```

`'email'` contains `m` ⇒ a `{ type: 'text', format: 'email' }` field — which `resolveCellRendererType` (`packages/fields/src/index.tsx:2915-2946`) honours as a `mailto:` renderer hint — is instead sent to `formatDate('ada@example.com', 'email')`. The reporting round ran the real `formatDate` from the pinned `packages/core/src/utils/date-display.ts` and got an **em dash**: the value is hidden in the dashboard `ObjectDataTable` and `RecordDetailDrawer`. A `format: 'money'` text value takes the same branch.

⚠️ The em-dash result is the reporting round's probe (branch selection replicated, `formatDate` imported); the filing seat re-read the branch at source but did ⛔ not re-run the probe.

## A failing probe to write

`renderFieldValue('ada@example.com', buildFieldMeta({ accessorKey: 'email_addr', def: { type: 'text', format: 'email' } }))` must not return the em dash.

## Context — why the two readers disagree

One `format` key is read by several renderers with different vocabularies: `resolveCellRendererType` treats a small word set as renderer hints on textual types; this branch treats any string containing a date letter as a date pattern. Whether that key should have a declared vocabulary is an open contract-shape question in objectstack (#19679's reserved decision) — ⛔ not this card. This card is only the collision: a hint word that is also matched as a date pattern.
